column1: # gate_first_refusal.tsv — FR-022 FIRST-REFUSAL registry (§11.4.115(F)).
# A gate newly bound to a seam is UNVALIDATED INSTRUMENTATION until it has
# been OBSERVED REFUSING at least once on a genuinely-broken input. Until
# that observation is recorded here, the gate contributes NO PASS to any
# suite result — an unobserved guard proves nothing, and counting its PASS
# would be a §11.4 PASS-bluff at the instrumentation layer.
# Schema (TAB-separated, 3 columns, one row per gate token):
#   <gate-token>\t<mutation-test-path>\t<observed-red-evidence-path>
#   <gate-token>                 the gate's own CM-* token, exactly as the
#                                gate assigns it to its `GATE=` variable.
#   <mutation-test-path>         the paired §1.1 mutation that flips the gate
#                                to FAIL. Repo-root-relative.
#   <observed-red-evidence-path> a recorded, NON-EMPTY transcript of that
#                                mutation actually being run and the gate
#                                actually refusing. Repo-root-relative.
#                                `PENDING-FIRST-REFUSAL` = not yet observed.
# `PENDING-FIRST-REFUSAL`, an empty field, a path that does not resolve, and
# a zero-byte file are ALL refusals — never "unobserved but acceptable"
# (§11.4.201(6): a missing observation is not an observation; §11.4.6: an
# absence is never silently upgraded into a pass).
# Lines beginning with `#` and blank lines are comments.
# Seeded (measured 2026-08-21) with the gates this feature wires whose paired
# mutation ALREADY EXISTS on disk. Their evidence is PENDING because the
# mutation runs are separate, later tasks — recording an evidence path before
# the run happened would be exactly the fabrication FR-022 exists to stop.
# Gates whose mutation siblings do not yet exist are deliberately ABSENT from
# this file rather than carrying a placeholder row: an absent row already
# refuses, and a placeholder row would assert a mutation test that is not
# there.
